title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — अक्षरब्रह्मयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 8: The Imperishable Brahman
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/अक्षरब्रह्मयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥

The compound has two senses, and the text does not say which Arjuna means: an honorific, 'best of men', of the kind the epic gives its heroes (Arjuna himself is puruṣarṣabha, 'bull among men', at 2.15), or the title Kṛṣṇa claims for himself at 15.18, the Person beyond the Perishable and the Imperishable. sentences.l: That brahman — what [is it]? Adhyātma — what? Action — what, O Supreme Person? And what is called adhibhūta, and what is adhidaiva called?
sentences.i: What is that brahman? What is the individual self? What is action, Supreme Person? What is called material existence, and what is called the divine order?
sentences.n: This opens the chapter as Arjuna's question, continuing directly from the end of chapter 7, whose closing verses (7.29-30) first named these very terms — brahman, adhyātma, karman, adhibhūta, adhidaiva — without defining them; Kṛṣṇa answers each in turn at 8.3-4, in the same order Arjuna asks them here. Puruṣottama, 'highest of persons', is rendered 'Supreme Person' wherever it occurs; the word's own entry gives the two senses it can carry in Arjuna's mouth. Sandhi: तद्ब्रह्म is tat + brahma; किमध्यात्मं, प्रोक्तमधिदैवं and किमुच्यते all show a final -m simply written joined before a following vowel, with no phonetic change (kim+adhyātmam, proktam+adhidaivam, kim+ucyate).

sentences.l: Adhiyajña — how, who [is it] here in this body, O slayer of Madhu? And at the time of departure, how are you to be known by those of controlled mind?
sentences.i: How, and who, is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, Madhusūdana? And how are you to be known, at the time of death, by those whose minds are controlled?
sentences.n: Arjuna's question continues, now asking after adhiyajña, the fourth term named at the end of chapter 7 (7.30) but not yet defined, and adding a fifth question of his own — how Kṛṣṇa is to be recognized at the moment of death (prayāṇa-kāle), which this chapter returns to repeatedly (verses 5-13). Madhusūdana, 'slayer of Madhu', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa recalling his defeat of the demon Madhu. Sandhi: कोऽत्र is kaḥ + atra; देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन packs dehe + asmin (avagraha) + madhusūdana (no further change); ज्ञेयोऽसि is jñeyaḥ + asi.

sentences.t:
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥

akṣaram brahma paramam svabhāvaḥ adhyātmam ucyate |
bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karaḥ visargaḥ karma-saṃjñitaḥ ||

morph.gloss: the imperishable (a name for brahman, opposite of kṣara 'the perishable', verse 4; also 'syllable', a distinct sense used at verse 13; nom. sg. neut., predicate)
brahman, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut., subject)
highest, supreme (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with akṣaram)
one's own nature, essential being (svabhāva: nom. sg., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
adhyātma (nom./acc. sg. neut., predicate)
to speak (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is called'; final -m stays before the vowel u-, written joined)

coming forth, arising (third member; bhāva + udbhava: a + u → o)

to emit, send forth (visarga: 'emission, creative discharge', nom. sg., subject)

sentences.l: The imperishable, supreme, [is] brahman; own-nature is called adhyātma. That which causes the coming-into-existence of beings' existence, the emission, is called action.
sentences.i: Brahman is the supreme imperishable; one's own essential nature is called the individual self. The creative outpouring that causes beings to come into existence is called action.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa now answers Arjuna's first two questions from verses 1-2, in order: brahman is identified with akṣaram, 'the imperishable' (paramam, 'supreme', qualifying it); adhyātma is defined as svabhāva, 'one's own essential nature'. The third answer, on karman, follows in the second half: action is defined as visarga, the 'emission' or 'creative discharge', bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karaḥ, 'that which causes the existence of beings to arise' — the cosmic outflow of activity by which beings come into being, not merely ritual or moral action. Karman itself is translated throughout, unlike brahman, dharma, yoga, the guṇas and sāṃkhya, which stay untranslated. Sandhi: स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते packs svabhāvaḥ + adhyātmam (avagraha) + ucyate (joined, no change); भूतभावोद्भवकरो packs bhūta + bhāva + udbhava (a+u→o) + karaḥ (-aḥ before v- → -o).

sentences.t:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् ।
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥
sentences.tr:
adhibhūtam kṣaraḥ bhāvaḥ puruṣaḥ ca adhidaivatam |
adhiyajñaḥ aham eva atra dehe deha-bhṛtām vara ||

the perishable, perishable (opposite of akṣara, verse 3; nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ before bh- → -o)

and

body (loc. sg., 'in the body')
body (first compound member)
bearer, one who bears (deha-bhṛt: 'body-bearer, embodied being', gen. pl.)

sentences.l: Adhibhūta [is] the perishable state; and puruṣa [is] adhidaivata. Adhiyajña, here in the body, [is] I myself, indeed, O best of the embodied.
sentences.i: Material existence is the perishable state, and the Person is the divine order. And the lord of sacrifice, here in the body, is I myself, best of embodied beings.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa completes the answer: adhibhūta, 'material existence', is kṣaraḥ bhāvaḥ, 'the perishable state' — set against akṣara, 'the imperishable', of verse 3; adhidaiva (here spelled adhidaivatam) is identified with puruṣaḥ, 'the Person', traditionally read as the totality of the gods or of the sense-faculties viewed as divine; and adhiyajña, 'the lord of sacrifice', Kṛṣṇa identifies directly with himself, present within the body (dehe) — the fifth and last term named at 7.30, now defined. Deha-bhṛtāṃ vara, 'O best of embodied beings', addresses Arjuna as a representative of all embodied souls. Sandhi: पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् packs puruṣaḥ + ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) + adhidaivatam (a+a→ā); अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र packs adhiyajñaḥ + aham (avagraha) + eva + atra (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् ।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥

yaḥ prayāti saḥ mad-bhāvam yāti na asti atra saṃśayaḥ ||

sentences.l: And at the time of the end, remembering me alone, having released the body — who thus departs, he attains my state of being; there is no doubt here.
sentences.i: And at the moment of death, remembering me alone as he leaves the body, whoever departs thus attains my own being; of this there is no doubt.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's recurring theme, first raised by Arjuna's question at verse 2: what determines a person's fate at the moment of death is what is remembered then (cf. verses 6, 10, 13). Sandhi: नास्त्यत्र packs na + asti (nā-) + atra (-i+a-→-y a-); स is saḥ with its visarga dropped before the consonant m- (a fixed rule for the pronoun forms saḥ and eṣaḥ, which never take -o before a consonant).

sentences.l: Whatever state, remembering, he abandons the body at the end — that very [state] he attains, O son of Kuntī, always having been habituated to that state.
sentences.i: Whatever state a man remembers when he finally leaves the body, that very state he attains, Kaunteya, ever having been steeped in it.
sentences.n: This generalizes verse 5: the state one attains at death is always whatever bhāva, 'state of being', one is habituated to through life (sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ) — a principle Kṛṣṇa uses in verse 7 to urge constant remembrance of himself specifically. Yaṃ yaṃ ... taṃ tam, doubled relative and correlative pronouns, are the standard distributive construction, 'whatever ... that same' (cf. 7.21's yo yo ... tasya tasya). Sandhi: वापि is vā + api; त्यजत्यन्ते is tyajati + ante; तमेवैति packs tam + eva + eti (a+e→ai).

sentences.l: Therefore, at all times remember me and fight. With mind and intellect fixed on me, you shall go to me alone, without doubt.
sentences.i: So keep me in mind at all times, and fight. With your mind and intellect fixed on me, you will surely come to me, beyond doubt.
sentences.n: This draws the practical conclusion from verses 5-6: since one becomes at death whatever one has dwelt on in life, Arjuna should remember Kṛṣṇa constantly even while fighting. The whole second line is written in the source as a single unbroken string, मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम्, packing five words: mayi + arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ + mām + eva + eṣyasi + asaṃśayam. The vulgate text printed and drafted here ends the verse with असंशयम्, asaṃśayam, an adverbial accusative, 'you shall come to me, without doubt'; the BORI critical edition (GRETIL, Tokunaga-Smith) reads instead असंशयः, asaṃśayaḥ, nominative — 'you shall come to me; there is no doubt' — as a separate clause. This is a real vulgate/BORI variant (listed as such in parts.json); the vulgate reading is the one printed here.

sentences.l: By a mind disciplined by the yoga of practice, not going to another [object] — the supreme divine Person he attains, O son of Pṛthā, continually contemplating [him].
sentences.i: With a mind disciplined by the yoga of practice, not straying to any other object, one attains the supreme divine Person, Pārtha, by dwelling on him without ceasing.
sentences.n: Abhyāsa-yoga, 'the yoga of [repeated] practice', names the discipline of habituation urged in verses 6-7: a mind trained not to wander (an-anya-gāmin, 'not going elsewhere') and kept in constant contemplation (anucintayan) is what reaches paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyam, 'the supreme divine Person', the object first named at verse 4 as adhidaiva. Sandhi: नान्यगामिना is na + anya-gāminā; पार्थानुचिन्तयन् is pārtha + anucintayan.

sentences.l: The seer, the ancient, the ruler, smaller than the atom — [him] who meditates on, the ordainer of all, of inconceivable form, sun-colored, beyond darkness —
sentences.i: Whoever meditates on the ancient seer, the ruler, subtler than the subtlest atom, the sustainer of all, of inconceivable form, radiant as the sun, beyond the reach of darkness —
sentences.n: This begins a single sentence completed only at verse 10 (sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti, 'he attains that supreme Person'): a relative clause (yaḥ ... anusmaret, 'whoever meditates on') piling up epithets for the object of meditation. Both half-lines are written in the source as long fused strings with a break only after their first word: पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः packs purāṇam + anuśāsitāram + aṇoḥ + aṇīyāṃsam + anusmaret + yaḥ, and धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं packs dhātāram + acintya-rūpam + āditya-varṇam. Aṇor aṇīyāṃsam, 'smaller than the atom, subtler than the subtle', is a standard formula for the ungraspable minuteness of the supreme self. Unlike verses 10, 11 and 28, this verse's two long lines are drafted here as an ordinary two-line block, following the source's own line division.

sentences.t:
प्रयाणकाले मनसाचलेन ।
भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव ।
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् ।
स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
sentences.tr:
prayāṇa-kāle manasā acalena |
bhaktyā yuktaḥ yoga-balena ca eva |
bhruvoḥ madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak |
saḥ tam param puruṣam upaiti divyam ||

morph.gloss: departure, death (first compound member)
time (loc. sg., 'at the time of departure')
mind (manasā: instr. sg.; written joined before a-, no change)
unmoving, unwavering (acalena: instr. sg., agreeing with manasā)
devotion (instr. sg., 'with devotion')
to join, endow (yukta: past participle 'endowed with, possessed of', nom. sg.; -aḥ before y- → -o)
yoga, kept untranslated (first compound member)
power, strength (yoga-bala: 'the power of yoga', instr. sg.)
and
indeed (ca + e- → cai-)
eyebrow (bhruvoḥ: gen./loc. dual, 'of the two eyebrows'; -oḥ + m- → -or m-)
middle (madhye: loc. sg., 'in the middle')
breath, life-force (prāṇam: acc. sg., object of āveśya; written joined before ā-, no change)
to cause to enter, fix (āveśya: causative gerund 'having fixed, having directed')
correctly, properly (adverb)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before the consonant t-)
that (acc. sg. masc.)
higher, supreme (acc. sg. masc.)
the Person (puruṣam: acc. sg., object of upaiti; written joined before u-, no change)
to go to, attain (upaiti: present 3rd sg. 'attains')
divine (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)

sentences.l: At the time of departure, with unwavering mind, endowed with devotion, and by the power of yoga indeed, having fixed the breath correctly between the eyebrows — he attains that supreme divine Person.
sentences.i: At the hour of death, with a mind that does not waver, filled with devotion, and by the strength of yoga, fixing the breath rightly between the eyebrows, he reaches that supreme, divine Person.
sentences.n: This completes the sentence begun in verse 9, describing the practice by which the object of meditation described there is reached: an unwavering mind (manasā acalena), devotion (bhaktyā), the power of yoga, and the yogic technique of fixing the breath between the eyebrows at death (bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya) — the same moment of death addressed since verse 5. This is the chapter's first four-line verse (triṣṭubh meter rather than the ordinary two-line śloka), so its words.txt block has three line-breaks rather than one. Sandhi: मनसाचलेन is manasā + acalena; भ्रुवोर्मध्ये is bhruvoḥ + madhye; प्राणमावेश्य is prāṇam + āveśya; पुरुषमुपैति is puruṣam + upaiti.

sentences.t:
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति ।
विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः ।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति ।
तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥
sentences.tr:
yat akṣaram veda-vidaḥ vadanti |
viśanti yat yatayaḥ vīta-rāgāḥ |
yat icchantaḥ brahma-caryam caranti |
tat te padam saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye ||

morph.gloss: which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative; -t + a- → -d a-)
the imperishable (akṣaram: acc. sg., object of vadanti; cf. verse 3)
the Veda (first compound member)
knowing, a knower (veda-vid: 'knower of the Veda', nom. pl., subject; -aḥ before v- → -o)
to speak, declare (present 3rd pl.)
to enter (present 3rd pl.)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, repeated; -t + y- → -d y-)
the ascetic, one who strives (yatayaḥ: nom. pl., subject; -aḥ before v- → -o)
to go, depart (vīta: past participle, first compound member, 'gone, departed')
passion, attachment (vīta-rāga: 'free from passion', nom. pl., agreeing with yatayaḥ)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, repeated a third time; -t + i- → -d i-)
to wish, desire (icchant: present participle 'desiring', icchantaḥ: nom. pl.; -aḥ before b- → -o)
brahman, kept untranslated (first compound member)
conduct, practice, discipline (brahma-carya: 'the discipline pertaining to brahman', i.e. chastity, religious studentship, acc. sg., object of caranti)
to practice, observe, live (present 3rd pl.)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of pravakṣye, referring to padam)
you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
place, state, goal (acc. sg., in apposition to tat)
to gather, sum up (saṃgraha: 'summary, compendium', instr. sg. adverbial, 'in brief, in summary')
to declare, proclaim (pravakṣye: future middle 1st sg. 'I shall declare')

sentences.l: Which imperishable the knowers of the Veda declare, which the passionless strivers enter, desiring which they practice the discipline of brahman (chastity) — that state to you in summary I shall declare.
sentences.i: That imperishable reality the knowers of the Veda speak of, that the passionless ascetics enter, that which seekers practice chastity to attain — I will now tell you that state in brief.
sentences.n: A triple-relative construction (yat ... yat ... yat, 'which ... which ... which', each governing a different verb) builds up a description of akṣara, 'the imperishable' — the same term brahman was identified with at verse 3 — before Kṛṣṇa announces he will now explain it 'in brief' (saṃgraheṇa), which he does through the rest of the chapter. Brahmacaryam, literally 'the discipline pertaining to brahman', is the traditional term for celibate religious studentship; brahman itself stays untranslated per convention, so the compound is rendered literally in L. This is the second of the chapter's three four-line (triṣṭubh) verses. Sandhi: यदक्षरं, यद्यतयो and यदिच्छन्तो each show yat losing its -t before the next consonant/vowel (-t+a-→-d a-; -t+y-→-d y-; -t+i-→-d i-); वेदविदो, यद्यतयो and यदिच्छन्तो all show a final -aḥ becoming -o before a voiced consonant.

sentences.t:
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-dvārāṇi saṃyamya manaḥ hṛdi nirudhya ca |
mūrdhni ādhāya ātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthitaḥ yoga-dhāraṇām ||

morph.gloss: all (first compound member)
gate, door (sarva-dvāra: 'all the gates [of the body, i.e. the senses]', acc. pl., object of saṃyamya)
to restrain, hold in check (gerund 'having restrained')
mind (acc. sg. neut., object of nirudhya; -aḥ before h- → -o)
heart (loc. sg., 'in the heart')
to confine, restrain (gerund 'having confined')
and
head, crown of the head (mūrdhni: loc. sg.; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
to place, fix upon (ādhāya: gerund 'having fixed', taking prāṇam as its object; ā + ā → ā)
self, own (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., 'of the self, one's own', qualifying prāṇam)
breath, life-force (prāṇam: acc. sg., object of ādhāya, 'having fixed [one's own] breath [on the head]'; written joined before ā-, no change)
to be established in, resort to (āsthita: past participle, nom. sg., governing the separate accusative yogadhāraṇām, 'established in yogic concentration'; -aḥ before y- → -o)
yoga, kept untranslated (first compound member)
concentration, fixation (yoga-dhāraṇā: 'yogic concentration', acc. sg., object of āsthitaḥ)

sentences.l: Having restrained all the gates, and confined the mind in the heart, and having fixed one's own breath in the head, established in yogic concentration —
sentences.i: Restraining every gate of the body, confining the mind within the heart, fixing the life-breath in the head, and settling into yogic concentration —
sentences.n: This begins the sentence completed at verse 13 (yaḥ prayāti ... sa yāti paramāṃ gatim, 'he who thus departs attains the supreme goal'), describing the yogic technique of dying consciously: withdrawing from the sense-gates (sarva-dvārāṇi), confining the mind in the heart, and raising the breath to the crown of the head (mūrdhni) — the same head-crown site implied at verse 10's 'between the eyebrows'. Sandhi: मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः packs mūrdhni + ādhāya (i+ā→yā) + ātmanaḥ (a+ā→ā); प्राणमास्थितो is prāṇam + āsthitaḥ.

sentences.t:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् ।
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
om iti eka-akṣaram brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran |
yaḥ prayāti tyajan deham saḥ yāti paramām gatim ||

morph.gloss: the syllable Om, the sacred monosyllable
thus (marking om as a quoted word; om + iti: written joined, no change)
one, single (first compound member; iti + eka: i + e → y e-)

syllable (a distinct sense from 'the imperishable' of verse 3, though traditionally felt as the same word, the 'imperishable syllable'; eka-akṣara: 'the single syllable', nom./acc. sg. neut., in apposition to brahma)
brahman, kept untranslated (nom./acc. sg. neut.)
to utter, pronounce (vyāharan: present participle 'uttering', nom. sg.; written joined before m-, no change)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me')
to remember (anusmaran: present participle 'remembering', nom. sg.; written joined before m-, no change)
who (nom. sg. masc. relative)
to go forth, depart (present 3rd sg.)
to abandon (tyajan: present participle 'abandoning', nom. sg.; written joined before d-, no change)
body (deham: acc. sg., object of tyajan)
he (visarga dropped before the consonant y-)
to go, attain (present 3rd sg.)
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
course, goal (acc. sg., object of yāti)

sentences.l: Om — thus the single-syllabled brahman — uttering, remembering me: who thus departs, abandoning the body, he attains the supreme goal.
sentences.i: Uttering the single syllable Om, that is brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs, leaving the body behind, reaches the highest goal.
sentences.n: Om, the sacred monosyllable used to open Vedic recitation (cf. 7.8's praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu, 'the syllable Om in all the Vedas'), is here called eka-akṣaram, 'the single syllable' — a different sense of akṣara from its use as 'the imperishable' at verses 3, 11 and 21, though the two senses are traditionally felt as one word, the syllable itself being 'imperishable'. This continues the death-meditation instructions of verses 10 and 12: uttering Om while remembering Kṛṣṇa, at the moment of leaving the body, leads to the supreme goal. Sandhi: ओमित्येकाक्षरं packs om + iti (joined) + eka-akṣaram (i+e→ye); व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् packs vyāharan + mām + anusmaran (all joined without change); त्यजन्देहं is tyajan + deham.

sentences.t:
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।
तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
sentences.tr:
ananya-cetāḥ satatam yaḥ mām smarati nityaśaḥ |
tasya aham sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ ||

morph.gloss: not other, undistracted (first compound member)
mind (ananya-cetas: 'whose mind is on nothing else', nom. sg.)
constantly, continually (adverb)
who (nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
to remember (present 3rd sg.)
perpetually, unceasingly, constantly (indeclinable adverb)
he, that (tasya: gen. sg. 'of him')
I (nom. sg., subject; a + a → ā)
easy to obtain (sulabha: nom. sg., predicate)
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
constant (first compound member)
to join, discipline (yukta: past participle, nitya-yukta: 'ever disciplined', gen. sg.)
the yogin, one who practices yoga (gen. sg., 'of the yogin')

sentences.l: Whose mind is on nothing else, who constantly, unceasingly remembers me — of him, I [am] easy to attain, O son of Pṛthā, of that ever-disciplined yogin.
sentences.i: For the yogin whose mind is fixed on nothing else, who remembers me constantly and without fail, I am easy to reach, Pārtha — for one who is always so disciplined.
sentences.n: This shifts from the moment of death to the discipline of a lifetime: ananya-cetāḥ, 'whose mind is on nothing else', and nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ, 'of the ever-disciplined yogin', describe the same constancy of remembrance urged since verse 7, now promised an easy reward (sulabhaḥ, 'easy to attain'). Sandhi: तस्याहं is tasya + aham (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् ।
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥
sentences.tr:
mām upetya punar-janma duḥkha-ālayam aśāśvatam |
na āpnuvanti mahā-ātmānaḥ saṃsiddhim paramām gatāḥ ||

morph.gloss: I (mām: acc. sg. 'me')
to reach, attain (upetya: gerund 'having reached'; written joined before u-, no change)
again (adverbial prefix; punaḥ retains its old -r form before voiced sounds rather than becoming -o)
birth (punar-janma: 'rebirth', acc. sg., object of āpnuvanti)
suffering, pain (first compound member)
abode, receptacle (duḥkha-ālaya: 'an abode of suffering', acc. sg. neut., in apposition to punarjanma; duḥkha + ā- → duḥkhā-)
not eternal, impermanent (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with duḥkhālayam; written joined before a-, no change)
not (na + ā- → nā-)
to obtain, attain (āpnuvanti: present 3rd pl.)
great (first compound member)
soul, self (mahā-ātman: 'great-souled', nom. pl., subject; ā + ā → ā)
to succeed, be accomplished (saṃsiddhi: 'complete accomplishment, perfection', acc. sg., object of gatāḥ)
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with saṃsiddhim)
to go (gata: past participle 'gone to, having attained', nom. pl., agreeing with mahātmānaḥ)

sentences.l: Having reached me, great souls, having attained the supreme perfection, do not obtain rebirth, an abode of suffering, not eternal.
sentences.i: Great souls who reach me, having attained the highest perfection, are not born again into this fleeting abode of suffering.
sentences.n: Punarjanma, 'rebirth', is defined here as duḥkha-ālayam aśāśvatam, 'an impermanent abode of suffering' — the fate that souls who attain Kṛṣṇa (mām upetya) and the highest perfection (saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ) escape, a claim the next verse contrasts with rebirth even in the highest heavens short of Kṛṣṇa himself. Sandhi: नाप्नुवन्ति is na + āpnuvanti (ā-); महात्मानः is mahā + ātmānaḥ (ā+ā→ā); दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् packs duḥkha + ālayam (a+ā→ā) + aśāśvatam (joined, no change).

sentences.t:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन ।
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
ā-brahma-bhuvanāt lokāḥ punaḥ āvartinaḥ arjuna |
mām upetya tu kaunteya punar-janma na vidyate ||

morph.gloss: up to, as far as (prefix)
Brahmā, the creator-god, here in the deity sense (as at verse 17), not the untranslated absolute of verses 3/11/24 (second compound member)
world, realm (brahma-bhuvana: 'the world of Brahmā', abl. sg. 'from/up to the world of Brahmā'; -āt + l- → -āl l-)
world (lokāḥ: nom. pl., subject, 'the worlds')
again (punaḥ retains -r before the vowel ā-: punar āvartinaḥ)
to turn back, return (āvartin: 'one who returns', āvartinaḥ: nom. pl., predicate, 'subject to return'; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
Arjuna (vocative)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me')
to reach, attain (upetya: gerund 'having reached'; written joined before u-, no change)
but
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
again
birth (punar-janma: 'rebirth', nom. sg., subject)
not
to find, exist (vidyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is found, exists')

sentences.l: The worlds up to the world of Brahmā [are] subject to return again, O Arjuna; but having reached me, O son of Kuntī, rebirth does not exist.
sentences.i: All the worlds, up to the world of Brahmā, are worlds one returns from, Arjuna; but for one who reaches me, Kaunteya, there is no rebirth.
sentences.n: This confirms verse 15 by contrast: even ā-brahma-bhuvanāt lokāḥ, 'the worlds as far as the world of Brahmā' — the highest heavens attainable by ordinary merit, including Brahmā's own realm — are punar-āvartinaḥ, 'subject to return', still within the cycle of rebirth; only reaching Kṛṣṇa himself (mām upetya) ends it, restating punar-janma na vidyate, 'there is no rebirth', in the same terms as verse 15's escape from duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam. Sandhi: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः is ā-brahma-bhuvanāt + lokāḥ (-āt+l-→-āl l-); पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन packs punar + āvartinaḥ (avagraha before arjuna).

sentences.t:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः ।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
sentences.tr:
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahaḥ yat brahmaṇaḥ viduḥ |
rātrim yuga-sahasra-antām te ahaḥ-rātra-vidaḥ janāḥ ||

morph.gloss: a thousand (first compound member)
an age, cosmic era (second member)
extent, limit, ending (sahasra-yuga-paryanta: 'having a thousand ages as its limit', acc. sg. neut.; written joined before a-, no change)
day (ahaḥ: nom. sg. neut., subject; before a following vowel or voiced consonant the stem surfaces as ahar-, an irregular retention of -r rather than the ordinary -aḥ→-o rule: ahar yat)
which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative; -t + b- → -d b-)
Brahmā, the creator-god, kept untranslated as a form of the same word brahman (brahmaṇaḥ: gen. sg. 'of Brahmā'; -aḥ before v- → -o)
to know (perfect 3rd pl. 'they know')
night (acc. sg., subject of an implied 'they know' carried over from the first half)
an age (first compound member)
a thousand (second member)
end, limit (yuga-sahasra-anta: 'having a thousand ages as its end', acc. sg. fem., agreeing with rātrim; a + a → ā)
they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject; te + a- → te with avagraha)
day (ahaḥ: first compound member; the stem surfaces as aho- before the following voiced r-, by the same irregular rule as ahaḥ in the first half)
night (second member)
knowing, a knower (ahaḥ-rātra-vid: 'a knower of day and night', vidaḥ: nom. pl.; -aḥ before j- → -o)
person, people (nom. pl., subject)

sentences.l: Which day, having a thousand ages as its limit, [is] Brahmā's — they know; and the night, having a thousand ages as its end — those people [are] the knowers of day and night.
sentences.i: The day of Brahmā, they know, lasts a thousand ages, and his night lasts as long — those who understand this understand what day and night truly are.
sentences.n: Brahmaṇaḥ, 'of Brahmā' (the creator-god), and brahman, the untranslated absolute of verses 3 and 24, are the same word in different senses — here specifically the personal creator-deity, whose single day (a kalpa) and single night each last sahasra-yuga-paryantam, 'a thousand cosmic ages', a scale against which the death-and-rebirth described in verses 15-16 is measured. Sandhi: the whole first half-line is written as one fused string, सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो, packing sahasra-yuga-paryantam + ahaḥ (as ahar- before the vowel-initial yat) + yat (-t+b-→-d b-) + brahmaṇaḥ (-aḥ before v- → -o); तेऽहोरात्रविदो packs te (avagraha) + ahaḥ (as aho- before r-) + rātra + vidaḥ (-aḥ before j- → -o).

sentences.t:
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे ।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥
sentences.tr:
avyaktāt vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanti ahaḥ-āgame |
rātri-āgame pralīyante tatra eva avyakta-saṃjñake ||

morph.gloss: unmanifest (avyaktāt: abl. sg. neut., 'from the unmanifest'; -āt + v- → -ād v-)
manifestation, manifest existence (vyaktayaḥ: nom. pl., subject)
all (nom. pl. fem., agreeing with vyaktayaḥ)
to come forth, arise (prabhavanti: present 3rd pl.; -i + a- → -y a-)
day (ahaḥ: first compound member, surfacing as ahar- before the following vowel)
to come, arrive (āgama: 'coming, arrival', āgame: loc. sg., 'at the coming of day')
night (rātri: stem in compound-like locative use; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
to come, arrive (āgame: loc. sg., 'at the coming of night')
to dissolve, merge back (present middle 3rd pl.)
there, in that (tatra + eva: a + e → ai)
precisely, that very (eva + avyakta: a + a → ā)
unmanifest (first compound member)
to name, call (saṃjñaka: 'called, named', avyakta-saṃjñaka: 'called "the unmanifest"', loc. sg., agreeing with tatra eva)

sentences.l: From the unmanifest, all manifestations arise, at the coming of day; at the coming of night, they dissolve, into that very [same principle] called 'the unmanifest'.
sentences.i: At the break of day, all manifest things spring forth from the unmanifest; at the fall of night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest state.
sentences.n: This turns from the day and night of Brahmā (verse 17) to a smaller-scale cosmic cycle: at each 'day', all vyaktayaḥ, 'manifestations' (created things), emerge from avyakta, 'the unmanifest' (a term returned to at verses 20-21 as a name for the ultimate reality beyond even this cycle); at each 'night' they dissolve back into it. Sandhi: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः is avyaktāt + vyaktayaḥ (-āt+v-→-ād v-); प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे packs prabhavanti (-i+a-→-y a-) + ahaḥ (as ahar- before the vowel ā-); रात्र्यागमे is rātri + āgame (i+ā→yā); तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके packs tatra + eva (a+e→ai) + avyakta (a+a→ā) + saṃjñake.

sentences.t:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
sentences.tr:
bhūta-grāmaḥ saḥ eva ayam bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate |
rātri-āgame avaśaḥ pārtha prabhavati ahaḥ-āgame ||

morph.gloss: being, creature (first compound member)
multitude, mass, collection (bhūta-grāma: 'the multitude of beings', nom. sg., subject)
that (nom. sg. masc., visarga dropped before the vowel e-)
the very same, indeed
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc.; eva + a- → evā-)
to be, come into existence (gerund 'having come into being')
to be, come into existence (repeated, 'again and again')
to dissolve (present middle 3rd sg.)

'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
to come forth, arise (prabhavati: present 3rd sg.; -i + a- → -y a-)
day (ahaḥ: surfacing as ahar- before the vowel ā-)
to come, arrive (āgame: loc. sg., 'at the coming of day')

sentences.l: That very same multitude of beings, having come into existence again and again, dissolves, powerless, O son of Pṛthā, at the coming of night, [and] comes forth again at the coming of day.
sentences.i: This same host of beings, coming into existence over and over, helplessly dissolves at nightfall and springs forth again at daybreak, Pārtha.
sentences.n: This restates verse 18 with the emphasis on the beings' own helplessness: avaśaḥ, 'without control, powerless', describes the bhūta-grāmaḥ, 'multitude of beings', caught in this cycle of arising and dissolving, in contrast to the unconditioned freedom Kṛṣṇa promised at verses 15-16 to those who reach him. Sandhi: एवायं is eva + ayam; रात्र्यागमेऽवशः packs rātri + āgame (i+ā→yā) + avaśaḥ (avagraha); प्रभवत्यहरागमे as in verse 18.

sentences.t:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः ।
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
paraḥ tasmāt tu bhāvaḥ anyaḥ avyaktaḥ avyaktāt sanātanaḥ |
yaḥ saḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati ||

morph.gloss: beyond, higher (paraḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that (tasmāt: abl. sg. neut. adverbial, 'than that, beyond that')
but (written joined, no change)
state, existence (bhāvaḥ: nom. sg., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
other, different (anyaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
unmanifest (avyaktaḥ: nom. sg., agreeing with bhāvaḥ; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
unmanifest (avyaktāt: abl. sg., 'than the unmanifest', i.e. beyond the unmanifest of verses 18-19)
eternal, everlasting (sanātanaḥ: nom. sg., agreeing with bhāvaḥ)
which (nom. sg. masc. relative)
that (nom. sg. masc., visarga dropped before s-)
all (loc. pl.)
being (loc. pl., 'among all beings')
to perish (naśyat: present participle 'perishing', naśyatsu: loc. pl., agreeing with bhūteṣu)
not
to perish, be destroyed (present 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: But beyond that there is another state, unmanifest, beyond the unmanifest, eternal — which, among all beings perishing, does not perish.
sentences.i: But beyond that cycle there is another reality, unmanifest, beyond even the unmanifest, everlasting — which does not perish when all beings perish.
sentences.n: Tasmāt, 'than that', refers back to the whole cycle of manifestation and dissolution of verses 18-19; this bhāvaḥ anyaḥ avyaktaḥ, 'another state, [also called] unmanifest', is explicitly distinguished from that avyaktāt, 'unmanifest' (the same word used again, now for a second, higher reality) — a distinction the next verse names directly as akṣara, 'the imperishable'. Sandhi: परस्तस्मात्तु is paraḥ + tasmāt (-aḥ+t-→-as t-) + tu; भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः packs bhāvaḥ + anyaḥ + avyaktaḥ (each -aḥ+a-→-o with avagraha) + avyaktāt + sanātanaḥ (no further change, t+s stays).

sentences.t:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
sentences.tr:
avyaktaḥ akṣaraḥ iti uktaḥ tam āhuḥ paramām gatim |
yam prāpya na nivartante tat dhāma paramam mama ||

morph.gloss: unmanifest (avyaktaḥ: nom. sg., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
the imperishable (akṣaraḥ: nom. sg., predicate, cf. verse 3; final visarga dropped before the following vowel i- of iti, kept as a separate word in the source)
thus (closing the preceding predication; iti + uktaḥ: i + u → y u-)
to speak, call (ukta: past participle 'called, termed', uktaḥ: nom. sg., agreeing with avyaktaḥ; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of āhuḥ, referring back to avyaktaḥ akṣaraḥ; written joined before ā-, no change)
to say, call (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. 'they call')
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
goal, course (acc. sg., in apposition to tam)
which (acc. sg. masc. relative, object of prāpya)
to reach, attain (gerund 'having reached')
not
to turn back, return (present middle 3rd pl.)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t + dh- → -d dh-)
abode, dwelling (dhāma: nom. sg. neut.)
highest, supreme (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with dhāma)
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my')

sentences.l: The unmanifest, called 'the imperishable' — that they call the supreme goal. Having attained which, they do not turn back — that [is] my supreme abode.
sentences.i: That unmanifest reality, called 'the imperishable', is what they call the highest goal; having reached it, none return — that is my highest abode.
sentences.n: This names the 'other, unmanifest state' of verse 20 directly: it is avyaktaḥ akṣaraḥ, 'the unmanifest, [also called] the imperishable' — the same akṣara that verse 3 identified with brahman — and Kṛṣṇa here calls it tad dhāma paramaṃ mama, 'my own supreme abode'. Sandhi: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर is avyaktaḥ + akṣaraḥ (-aḥ+a-→-o with avagraha); the visarga of akṣaraḥ itself, before the vowel इति that begins the next word, simply drops without further vowel fusion, which is why the source keeps a space here rather than merging the two words further; इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः packs iti + uktaḥ (i+u→yu) + tam (-aḥ+t-→-as t-) + āhuḥ (joined); तद्धाम is tat + dhāma (-t+dh-→-d dh-).

sentences.t:
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
sentences.tr:
puruṣaḥ saḥ paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyaḥ tu ananyayā |
yasya antaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idam tatam ||

morph.gloss: the Person (nom. sg., subject)
that (nom. sg. masc.)
higher, supreme (nom. sg., agreeing with puruṣaḥ)
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
devotion (instr. sg., 'by devotion')
to obtain (labhya: gerundive 'to be obtained, attainable', nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
but, however (tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)
not other, exclusive, undivided (ananyayā: instr. sg. fem., agreeing with bhaktyā, 'by undivided devotion')
who (yasya: gen. sg. masc. relative, 'of whom, within whom'; a + a → ā)
standing within, dwelling within (antaḥ-sthāni: nom. pl. neut., predicate, agreeing with bhūtāni)
being, creature (nom. pl. neut., subject)
by whom (instr. sg. masc. relative)
all (sarvam: nom. sg. neut.)
this (idam: nom. sg. neut., in apposition, 'all this [universe]', subject of tatam)
to stretch, extend, pervade (tata: past participle 'stretched out, pervaded', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: That Person is supreme, O son of Pṛthā, attainable by undivided devotion — within whom beings dwell, by whom this all is pervaded.
sentences.i: That supreme Person, Pārtha, can be reached only through undivided devotion — the one within whom all beings dwell, and by whom this whole universe is pervaded.
sentences.n: This returns to puruṣaḥ, 'the Person', last named at verse 8 as the goal of unwavering practice, now specified as reachable bhaktyā tu ananyayā, 'only by undivided devotion' — echoing 7.17's eka-bhaktiḥ, 'single-minded devotion' — and described in terms recalling 7.7's image of the world strung on Kṛṣṇa like jewels on a thread (yasya antaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṃ tatam). Sandhi: लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया packs labhyaḥ (-aḥ+t-→-as t-) + tu (u+a→va, yaṇ) + ananyayā; यस्यान्तःस्थानि is yasya + antaḥsthāni (a+a→ā); सर्वमिदं is sarvam + idam.

sentences.t:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः ।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
sentences.tr:
yatra kāle tu anāvṛttim āvṛttim ca eva yoginaḥ |
prayātāḥ yānti tam kālam vakṣyāmi bharata-ṛṣabha ||

morph.gloss: where, in which (relative adverb)
time (loc. sg., 'at the time')
but (tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)
non-return (anāvṛtti: 'non-return', anāvṛttim: acc. sg., object of yānti)
return (āvṛtti: acc. sg., object of yānti, coordinated with anāvṛttim; written joined before ā-, no change)
and
indeed (ca + e- → cai-)
the yogin (nom. pl., subject)
to go forth, depart (prayāta: past participle 'having departed', nom. pl.; visarga dropped before the voiced y- of yānti)
to go, attain (present 3rd pl.)
that (acc. sg. masc.)
time (acc. sg., object of vakṣyāmi)
to speak, declare (future 1st sg. 'I shall declare')
descendant of Bharata (first compound member)
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative, addressed to Arjuna; a + ṛ- → ar-)

sentences.l: At which time, but, to non-return and to return as well, yogins, having departed, go — that time I shall declare, O bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.i: The time at which yogins depart to reach non-return, and the time at which they depart and return again — that time I will now explain to you, bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.n: This announces the topic of verses 24-26: the two 'times' or 'paths' of departure from the body, one leading to anāvṛtti, 'non-return' (freedom from rebirth), the other to āvṛtti, 'return' (rebirth) — a teaching Kṛṣṇa says he will now declare (vakṣyāmi), picking up the promise of verse 11 to explain akṣara saṃgraheṇa, 'in brief'. Sandhi: त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं packs tu (u+a→va) + anāvṛttim + āvṛttim (joined); प्रयाता is prayātāḥ with its visarga dropped before यान्ति (voiced y-).

sentences.t:
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
sentences.tr:
agniḥ jyotiḥ ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṭ-māsāḥ uttara-ayanam |
tatra prayātāḥ gacchanti brahma brahma-vidaḥ janāḥ ||

morph.gloss: fire (agniḥ: nom. sg., first item of the list; -iḥ + j- → -ir j-)
light, flame (jyotiḥ: nom. sg., second item; -iḥ + a- → -ir)
day (ahaḥ: nom. sg. neut., third item)
bright, white; the bright [fortnight of the waxing moon] (nom. sg., fourth item)
six (first compound member; compound stem ṣaṭ-, assimilated to ṣaṇ- before m-)
month (ṣaṇ-māsāḥ: 'the six months', nom. pl., fifth item; visarga dropped before the vowel u- of uttarāyaṇam)
northern, higher (first compound member)
course, path (uttara-ayana: 'the northern course [of the sun]', nom. sg. neut.; a + a → ā)
there, at that [time]
to go forth, depart (prayāta: past participle, nom. pl.; visarga dropped before the voiced g- of gacchanti)
to go (present 3rd pl.)
brahman, kept untranslated (acc. sg. neut., object of gacchanti)
brahman, kept untranslated (first compound member)
knowing, a knower (brahma-vid: 'knower of brahman', nom. pl., subject; -aḥ before j- → -o)
person, people (nom. pl., in apposition to brahmavidaḥ)

sentences.l: Fire, light, day, the bright [fortnight], the six months of the northern course — there departing, they go to brahman, the people who are knowers of brahman.
sentences.i: Fire, light, day, the bright half of the month, the six months of the sun's northern course — departing at such a time, those who know brahman go to brahman.
sentences.n: This gives the path of non-return promised in verse 23: a list of five ascending markers — fire, light, day, the bright (waxing) fortnight, and the six months of the sun's northern course (uttarāyaṇa, when the sun appears to move northward) — traditionally read as the successive stages of the 'path of the gods', by which brahma-vidaḥ, 'knowers of brahman', reach brahman itself without return. Sandhi: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः packs agniḥ (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-) + jyotiḥ (-iḥ+a-→-ir); षण्मासा is ṣaṭ + māsāḥ (-ṭ+m-→-ṇ m-) with its own visarga then dropped before उत्तरायणम्; उत्तरायणम् is uttara + ayanam (a+a→ā); प्रयाता is prayātāḥ, visarga dropped before गच्छन्ति; ब्रह्मविदो is brahma-vidaḥ, -aḥ before j- → -o.

sentences.t:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
sentences.tr:
dhūmaḥ rātriḥ tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṭ-māsāḥ dakṣiṇa-ayanam |
tatra cāndramasam jyotiḥ yogī prāpya nivartate ||

night (rātriḥ: nom. sg., second item; -iḥ + t- → -is t-)
likewise, and (adverb)
dark, black; the dark [fortnight of the waning moon] (nom. sg., third item)
six (first compound member)
month (ṣaṇ-māsāḥ: 'the six months', nom. pl., fourth item; visarga dropped before the voiced d- of dakṣiṇāyanam)
southern (first compound member)

sentences.l: Smoke, night, likewise, the dark [fortnight], the six months of the southern course — there, having reached the lunar light, the yogin returns.
sentences.i: Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months of the sun's southern course — by that path the yogin reaches the light of the moon, and returns.
sentences.n: This gives the counterpart path of return: smoke, night, the dark (waning) fortnight, and the six months of the sun's southern course (dakṣiṇāyana) — traditionally the 'path of the ancestors' — by which a yogin reaches only cāndramasaṃ jyotiḥ, 'the light of the moon' (a lesser, temporary heaven), and then nivartate, 'returns' to rebirth, unlike the brahma-vidaḥ of verse 24. Sandhi: धूमो is dhūmaḥ, -aḥ before r- → -o; रात्रिस्तथा is rātriḥ + tathā (-iḥ+t-→-is t-); षण्मासा as in verse 24; दक्षिणायनम् is dakṣiṇa + ayanam (a+a→ā); ज्योतिर्योगी is jyotiḥ + yogī (-iḥ+y-→-ir y-).

sentences.t:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः ॥
sentences.tr:
śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī hi ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate |
ekayā yāti anāvṛttim anyayā āvartate punaḥ ||

dark, black (śukla-kṛṣṇe: 'the bright and the dark [paths]', nom. dual)
path, course (nom. dual, subject)

sentences.l: Bright and dark — these two [are] the world's eternal paths, so held; by one, [the soul] goes to non-return, by the other it returns again.
sentences.i: The bright path and the dark — these two are held to be the world's everlasting courses; by one the soul goes to no return, by the other it comes back again.
sentences.n: This sums up verses 24-25 by naming the two courses śukla and kṛṣṇa, 'bright' and 'dark', as jagataḥ śāśvate gatī mate, 'the world's two eternal paths', with ekayā ... anyayā, 'by one ... by the other', picking up each path's outcome directly from the preceding two verses. Sandhi: ह्येते is hi + ete (i+e→ye); यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते packs yāti (-i+a-→-y a-) + anāvṛttim + anyayā + āvartate (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥
sentences.tr:
na ete sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana |
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yuktaḥ bhava arjuna ||

this (ete: acc. dual masc., object of jānan, 'these two [paths]')
path, course (acc. dual, in apposition to ete)
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
to know (jānan: present participle 'knowing', nom. sg.; written joined before y-, no change)

sentences.l: Not these two paths, knowing, is the yogin confused, any at all, O son of Pṛthā; therefore, at all times, be disciplined in yoga, O Arjuna.
sentences.i: No yogin who knows these two paths is ever confused, Pārtha; so at all times remain disciplined in yoga, Arjuna.
sentences.n: This closes the teaching on the two paths (sṛtī, another word for 'path', echoing gatī of verse 26): knowing them removes all confusion for a yogin, and Kṛṣṇa draws the same practical conclusion as verse 7 — constant discipline in yoga at every moment. Sandhi: नैते is na + ete; तस्मात्सर्वेषु as in verse 7; योगयुक्तो is yoga-yuktaḥ, -aḥ before bh- → -o; भवार्जुन is bhava + arjuna (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव ।
दानेषु यत् पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् ।
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा ।
योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥

dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalam pradiṣṭam |

yogī param sthānam upaiti ca ādyam ||

sentences.l: Whatever meritorious fruit is declared [to belong] to [rites of] the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts — the yogin, having known all this, goes beyond [it] and attains the supreme, primal station.
sentences.i: Whatever reward is promised for the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and acts of giving, the yogin, knowing all this, transcends it and reaches the supreme, primal abode.
sentences.n: The chapter's closing, third four-line verse sums up its whole argument: the merits promised for the Vedic disciplines named here — study of the Vedas, sacrifice, austerity, giving — are all finite (cf. 7.23's antavat phalam), and the yogin who has understood everything taught since verse 5 goes beyond them all (atyeti) to param sthānam ādyam, 'the supreme, primal station' — Kṛṣṇa's own abode named at verse 21. Sandhi: चैव is ca + eva; तत्सर्वमिदं packs tat + sarvam + idam (all joined without change); स्थानमुपैति is sthānam + upaiti; चाद्यम् is ca + ādyam (a+ā→ā).

about: Chapter 8, Akṣarabrahmayoga, "the yoga of the imperishable brahman," opens with Arjuna asking seven rapid questions left over from the close of chapter 7: what are brahman, the individual self, action, material existence, the divine order, and the lord of sacrifice, and how is Kṛṣṇa to be known at the moment of death? Kṛṣṇa answers the first six in two terse verses, identifying brahman with akṣara, "the imperishable," and defining each remaining term in turn, before turning to the seventh question, which occupies the rest of the chapter: what happens at death. His answer is that a person becomes, at death, whatever state of mind they have dwelt on throughout life, so that constant remembrance of Kṛṣṇa, sustained through the discipline of yoga, determines the outcome; several verses describe the yogic technique of dying consciously, fixing the breath between the eyebrows or at the crown of the head while uttering the sacred syllable Om. Kṛṣṇa then contrasts the fate of those who reach him, final release from rebirth, with even the highest heavens short of that goal, which remain subject to return, on a cosmic timescale measured in Brahmā's single day and night of a thousand ages each. The chapter closes by naming two paths a departed soul may take, one of fire, day and the sun's northern course leading to no return, the other of smoke, night and its southern course leading back to rebirth, and ends by declaring that the yogin who understands all this surpasses even the rewards of Vedic ritual and reaches the supreme, primal abode.
